breakfast.name: Doubles
ingredients: Channa: chickpeas, curry, cumin, scotch bonnet
instructions: Make bara dough, fry thin rounds
Cook curried chickpeas
Place channa between two bara
Add chutneys to taste
breakfast.description: Trinidad's iconic street food — curried chickpeas in fried dough.

breakfast.name: Bake and Shark
instructions: Fry bakes until puffy
Season and fry shark fillet
Stuff bake with shark and all the chutneys
breakfast.description: Fried shark in fried bread with every sauce available.

breakfast.name: Doubles (Bara with Channa)
ingredients: Bara (small fried flatbreads: flour, yeast, turmeric, cumin)
Channa (curried chickpeas: onion, garlic, cumin, shadow beni, chilli)
instructions: Doubles is the Trinidadian street breakfast and the national street food
Two bara (fried flatbreads) + channa (curried chickpeas)
The name: you get double bara -- hence "doubles"
Invented in the 1930s by Emamool Deen -- a Trinidadian Indian food vendor
Now the most popular street food in Trinidad
Sold from small carts or stands from 5am
Customized with: pepper (how much?), tamarind, kuchela (mango achaar)
Eaten in hand, the bara softening from the channa
The best doubles: soft bara, well-curried channa, plenty of pepper sauce
breakfast.description: Trinidadian national street food -- two fried turmeric-cumin flatbreads (bara) topped with curried chickpeas (channa), pepper sauce, and kuchela (mango pickle). Invented in the 1930s by Emamool Deen. Sold from carts from 5am. "Doubles" because you always get two bara.

breakfast.name: Accra (Saltfish Fritters)
ingredients: Saltfish (dried salted cod -- soaked to desalt)
instructions: Accra are the Trinidadian saltfish fritters -- also called bacalaitos in Puerto Rico
Saltfish (salt cod) soaked, shredded, and mixed into a flour batter
Deep-fried until golden and crispy
The saltfish gives a salty, briny, savory flavor
The salt cod tradition in the Caribbean: preserved fish from European (especially Portuguese and British) trade
Eaten for breakfast with hot sauce or with bake
breakfast.description: Trinidadian saltfish fritters -- soaked and shredded salt cod mixed into a flour batter with onion, chilli, and turmeric, deep-fried until crispy. Salt cod preservation reached the Caribbean through European trade. Eaten with hot sauce or bake.

lunch.name: Pelau
instructions: Brown sugar for caramel, add chicken
Add green seasoning, coconut milk, peas
Add rice and pumpkin
Cook covered until done
lunch.description: One-pot coconut rice — Trinidad's national dish.

lunch.name: Callaloo
instructions: Cook dasheen leaves until very soft
Add coconut milk, okra, crab, pumpkin
Blend with swizzle stick until thick and smooth
lunch.description: Thick, green, coconut crab soup — the other national dish.

lunch.name: Pelau (Rice with Pigeon Peas)
ingredients: Chicken or beef (caramelized in brown sugar first)
Onion, garlic, spring onion, celery, thyme
instructions: Pelau is the Trinidadian one-pot rice dish -- the Creole soul food
The technique: the meat is browned first in caramelized sugar (browning)
Browning: caramelizing sugar in a hot pot until dark amber-brown, then adding the meat
The sugar coats the meat and gives a deep, bittersweet caramel color
Rice, pigeon peas, and coconut milk go in -- everything cooked together
The final dish is savory, slightly sweet, fragrant
The browning is the Trinidadian technique that differentiates pelau from plain rice
lunch.description: Trinidadian caramelized sugar rice -- pelau, chicken browned in caramelized sugar (browning: the technique that defines it), cooked one-pot with rice, pigeon peas, and coconut milk. The browning gives the meat a deep, bittersweet coating. The Trinidadian Creole soul food.

lunch.name: Roti and Curry (Dhal Puri)
ingredients: Dhal puri (roti filled with split peas ground inside -- the ground dhal creates a flaky, tender texture)
Chutney: mango, tamarind, shadow beni (chadon beni: Caribbean coriander)
instructions: Trinidadian roti culture comes from the Indian indenture (1845-1917)
Indentured workers brought from India after the abolition of slavery
They brought their roti tradition -- which evolved in Trinidad
Dhal puri: the most popular Trinidadian roti -- a flatbread with ground split peas kneaded inside
The ground split peas give it a tender, flaky, almost layered texture
Wrapped around curry: chicken, goat, vegetable, or potato
Shadow beni (chadon beni/Eryngium foetidum -- sawtooth coriander): the Trinidadian herb that replaced Indian coriander
lunch.description: Trinidadian Indian-heritage dhal puri roti -- a flatbread with split peas ground inside (creating a tender, flaky texture), wrapped around curry. Brought by Indian indentured workers (1845-1917). Shadow beni (sawtooth coriander, the Trinidadian herb) is the key chutney herb.

lunch.name: Macaroni Pie
instructions: Macaroni pie is the Trinidadian Sunday lunch staple -- not American mac and cheese
A baked macaroni custard: pasta in an egg-milk custard with cheese
It sets firm like a quiche -- sliced into squares
Eaten as a side dish with stew chicken, callaloo, and pelau
The Sunday lunch combination in Trinidad: stew chicken + macaroni pie + callaloo + pelau
A Creole interpretation of European pasta dishes
lunch.description: Trinidadian baked macaroni custard -- elbow macaroni in an egg-evaporated milk custard with cheddar and sweet peppers, baked firm and sliced into squares. Not American mac and cheese: it sets like a quiche. The essential Sunday lunch side dish alongside stew chicken and callaloo.

dinner.name: Curry Goat Trini Style
instructions: Marinate goat with curry and seasoning overnight
Brown in oil
Add water, simmer 45 min
Add potatoes, cook until tender
Serve with roti or rice
dinner.description: Curried goat — rich, hot, and essential to any Trini lime.

dinner.name: Stew Chicken
instructions: Brown chicken with sugar-caramel
Add seasoning and browning sauce
Add ketchup and water
Simmer 25 min

dinner.name: Callaloo (Dasheen Leaf Soup)
ingredients: Onion, garlic, thyme, spring onion, shadow beni
instructions: Callaloo is the Trinidadian national dish -- the green stew made from dasheen leaves
Dasheen bush (taro leaves) cooked with okra in coconut milk
The okra gives the characteristic smooth, silky texture (mucilaginous)
Blue crab is the traditional protein addition -- gives a deep seafood flavor
Blended smooth at the end -- a thick green stew
Eaten at every Sunday lunch alongside macaroni pie and rice
dinner.description: Trinidadian taro leaf green stew -- dasheen bush (taro leaves) cooked with okra (the mucilage thickens), coconut milk, and blue crab into a thick, silky, smooth green stew. The national dish. Blended smooth at the end. At every Trinidad Sunday lunch alongside macaroni pie.

dinner.name: Stewed Chicken
ingredients: Green seasoning (garlic, onion, spring onion, shadow beni, thyme, pimento peppers -- blended)
instructions: Stewed chicken is the most common Trinidadian everyday dinner
The chicken is marinated in green seasoning -- the Trinidadian herb marinade
Green seasoning: a blended herb paste of shadow beni, thyme, spring onion, garlic, and pimento peppers
Then browned in caramelized sugar (browning)
Stewed until the sauce is thick and rich
dinner.description: Trinidadian everyday stewed chicken -- marinated in green seasoning (blended shadow beni, thyme, spring onion, garlic: the Trinidadian herb paste), browned in caramelized sugar, stewed in tomatoes until the sauce is thick and rich. The most common Trinidadian dinner.

dinner.name: Shark and Bake (Fried Shark Sandwich)
ingredients: Bake (fried bread: flour, baking powder, butter -- deep fried)
instructions: Shark and bake is the Maracas Beach specialty -- the beach food of Trinidad
Maracas Bay: the most popular beach in Trinidad
Fried shark fillet served in a bake (a fried bread roll)
Dressed with tamarind, pepper sauce, shadow beni, and fresh vegetables
The condiment selection at Maracas is part of the experience -- many choices
Richard's and Natalie's are the famous shark and bake vendors at Maracas
A pilgrimage destination for Trinidadians
dinner.description: Trinidadian Maracas Beach shark sandwich -- fried shark fillet in a bake (fried bread roll) with tamarind, pepper sauce, shadow beni, and vegetables. Maracas Bay is the pilgrimage beach; Richard's and Natalie's are the famous vendors. Going to Maracas for shark and bake is a Trinidadian rite.

snacks.name: Pholourie
instructions: Mix batter
Fry spoonfuls until golden
Serve with tamarind or mango chutney
snacks.description: Split pea fritters with tamarind chutney.

snacks.name: Pholourie (Split Pea Fritters)
ingredients: Yellow split peas (ground to flour or split pea flour)
instructions: Pholourie are the Trinidadian split pea fritters -- Indo-Trinidadian origin
A batter of split pea flour, turmeric, and cumin
Dropped into hot oil and fried into balls
Eaten with mango chutney or tamarind sauce
A quintessentially Indo-Trinidadian snack -- eaten at Hindu religious events
snacks.description: Trinidadian Indian-heritage split pea fritters -- pholourie, split pea flour batter with turmeric and cumin fried into golden balls, eaten with mango chutney or tamarind sauce. Indo-Trinidadian origin, eaten at Hindu religious events.

snacks.name: Kurma (Sweet Fried Dough)
instructions: Kurma is the Indo-Trinidadian sweet fried dough -- eaten at Divali and celebrations
Short pastry dough cut into strips and deep-fried
Crunchy and slightly sweet
Eaten at Divali (Diwali) and Hindu celebrations in Trinidad
The Indian indenture community brought this sweet from India
snacks.description: Trinidadian Indian-heritage sweet fried dough -- kurma, short pastry cut into strips and fried until crunchy. Eaten at Divali and Hindu celebrations in Trinidad. Brought by the Indian indenture community.

snacks.name: Solo (Sweet Aerated Drink)
ingredients: Solo (a Trinidadian carbonated drink -- various flavors: orange, cream soda, kola champagne)
instructions: Solo is the Trinidadian carbonated soft drink brand
A local institution since 1952
Made in several flavors: orange, cream soda, cherry, kola champagne
Kola champagne: a unique creamy cola flavor found in the Caribbean
Drunk at every Trinidadian event and cricket match
The national beverage alongside rum and coconut water
snacks.description: Trinidadian local soft drink -- Solo, a carbonated drink made in Trinidad since 1952 in flavors including orange, cream soda, and kola champagne (a creamy cola unique to the Caribbean). A national institution drunk at cricket matches and every Trinidadian event.

desserts.name: Kurma
instructions: Make stiff dough
Cut into small shapes
Deep fry until golden
Toss in sugar syrup with cardamom
desserts.description: Sweet fried dough in cardamom syrup — Indo-Trinidadian treat.

desserts.name: Gulab Jamun
instructions: Gulab jamun is the Indo-Trinidadian sweet -- directly from the Indian tradition
Milk solid dough balls fried until golden
Soaked in sugar syrup flavored with rosewater and cardamom
Eaten at Hindu celebrations: Divali, weddings, puja
The Indian sweet tradition preserved in Trinidad for generations
desserts.description: Trinidadian Indian-heritage milk sweet -- gulab jamun, milk powder dough balls fried golden and soaked in rosewater-cardamom sugar syrup. Directly from the Indian tradition, eaten at Divali, weddings, and puja. The Indian sweet tradition preserved in Trinidad for 180 years.

desserts.name: Black Cake (Rum Fruit Cake)
ingredients: Dried fruit (prunes, raisins, currants, cherries -- soaked in rum for weeks to months)
Browning sauce (caramelized sugar for the black color)
instructions: Trinidadian black cake is the Christmas cake
The dried fruit is soaked in rum for weeks -- or even a year for serious bakers
The browning (caramelized sugar) gives the near-black color
Dense, boozy, and rich
Made weeks before Christmas and aged
Each family recipe is a closely guarded secret
Related to British Christmas cake -- the Trinidadian version is much darker and richer
desserts.description: Trinidadian Christmas black cake -- dried fruit soaked in rum for weeks (or months), mixed with browning sauce (caramelized sugar for the near-black color), butter, and warm spices. Denser, darker, and richer than British Christmas cake. Aged weeks before Christmas. Each family recipe is a secret.

drinks.name: Sorrel Drink
instructions: Boil sorrel with ginger, cloves, orange peel
Strain, sweeten
Chill
drinks.description: Tart, spiced sorrel drink — a Christmas tradition.

drinks.name: Ponche de Crème
instructions: Blend eggs, milks, rum, lime zest, bitters
Strain
Grate nutmeg on top
Chill before serving
drinks.description: Trinidad's eggnog — rich, boozy, and bitters-spiked.

drinks.name: Sorrel Drink (Hibiscus)
ingredients: Dried sorrel (hibiscus calyces -- dried Hibiscus sabdariffa)
instructions: Sorrel is the Trinidadian Christmas drink -- made from dried hibiscus
In Trinidad, "sorrel" refers to the dried hibiscus calyx -- not the herb
Steeped in hot water with ginger and warm spices
Sweetened and chilled
The Christmas version: rum is added -- sorrel punch
The deep ruby color is beautiful
Drunk throughout the Caribbean at Christmas -- in Jamaica, Trinidad, Barbados
drinks.description: Trinidadian Christmas hibiscus drink -- sorrel (dried Hibiscus sabdariffa calyces) steeped in hot water with ginger, cloves, and cinnamon, sweetened and chilled. Deep ruby red. The Christmas version: rum added (sorrel punch). In Trinidad, sorrel = hibiscus, not the herb. Drunk across the Caribbean at Christmas.
